title: Genesis Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:1, what happened when men began to multiply on the earth?
options: The earth was filled with violence
The sons of God married the daughters of men
God commanded Noah to build an ark
questions.correctAnswer: Daughters were born unto them
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:1 states that when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, daughters were born unto them.

questions.question: Who saw that the daughters of men were fair and took them wives?
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of God
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:2 says the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair and took them wives of all which they chose.

questions.question: How long did the LORD say man's days would be, according to Genesis 6:3?
questions.correctAnswer: An hundred and twenty years
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:3 records the LORD saying man's days shall be an hundred and twenty years.

questions.question: What were present on the earth in the days mentioned in Genesis 6:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Giants
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:4 states that there were giants in the earth in those days.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:5, what was the condition of the imagination of man's heart?
questions.correctAnswer: Only evil continually
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:5 says every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was only evil continually.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 6:6 says that the LORD was pleased with the way He had made man on the earth.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:6 states that it repented the LORD that He had made man on the earth and it grieved Him at His heart, showing displeasure.

questions.question: What did the LORD decide to do to man and all living creatures, according to Genesis 6:7?
options: Destroy them from the face of the earth
Send a prophet to warn them
questions.correctAnswer: Destroy them from the face of the earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:7 records the LORD saying He will destroy man whom He has created from the face of the earth, including beasts and fowls.

questions.question: Who found grace in the eyes of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Noah
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:8 clearly says that Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 6:9, Noah was a just man and walked with God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:9 describes Noah as a just man, perfect in his generations, who walked with God.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of Noah's sons named in Genesis 6:10?
questions.correctAnswer: Cainan
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:10 lists Noah’s three sons as Shem, Ham, and Japheth; Cainan is not mentioned.

questions.question: True or False: In Genesis 6:11, the earth was described as being full of violence and corrupt before God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:11 states the earth was corrupt before God and filled with violence.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:12, why was the earth corrupt?
options: All flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth
The sons of God had taken wives
Noah had not yet been born
questions.correctAnswer: All flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:12 says God saw the earth was corrupt because all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth.

questions.question: In Genesis 6, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Make thee an ark of gopher wood
Bring two of every living thing into the ark
questions.correctAnswer: Make thee an ark of gopher wood
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:14 commands Noah first to make an ark of gopher wood before the other instructions come later.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:15, what is the length of the ark that Noah was commanded to build?
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred cubits
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:15 states the length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 6:16 instructs Noah to make the door of the ark on the top of it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:16 says the door of the ark shall be set in the side thereof, not on the top.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How does Genesis 6:9 describe Noah's character and conduct?
options: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and he walked with God
Noah was a wise man who built many cities
Noah was a mighty warrior who fought for his people
Noah was a prophet who foretold the flood
questions.correctAnswer: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and he walked with God
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:9 explicitly states Noah was just, perfect in his generations, and walked with God, highlighting his righteousness and close relationship with God, which contrasts with the corrupt world described in verses 11-12.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:10, who were the three sons of Noah?
questions.correctAnswer: Shem, Ham, and Japheth
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:10 clearly names Noah's three sons as Shem, Ham, and Japheth, who play significant roles in the biblical narrative following the flood.

questions.question: What does Genesis 6:11 say about the condition of the earth before the flood?
options: The earth was corrupt before God and filled with violence
The earth was peaceful and prosperous
The earth was covered in water
The earth was inhabited only by animals
questions.correctAnswer: The earth was corrupt before God and filled with violence
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:11 describes the earth as corrupt and filled with violence, indicating the moral decay and lawlessness that prompted God's judgment, as further emphasized in verses 12 and 13.

questions.question: What reason does Genesis 6:12 give for God's decision to destroy all flesh?
options: All flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:12 explains that the earth was corrupt because all flesh had corrupted its way, providing the basis for God's decision to bring destruction as described in verses 13 and 17.

questions.question: What specific instructions does God give Noah regarding the construction of the ark in Genesis 6:14?
options: Make the ark of gopher wood, with rooms, and pitch it inside and outside
Build the ark from cedar wood without rooms
Construct a large tent of animal skins
Build a stone house to withstand the flood
questions.correctAnswer: Make the ark of gopher wood, with rooms, and pitch it inside and outside
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:14 directs Noah to build the ark from gopher wood, to make rooms within it, and to seal it with pitch inside and outside, which was essential for its waterproofing as further detailed in verses 15 and 16.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:15, what are the dimensions of the ark that Noah was instructed to build?
options: Length: 300 cubits, Breadth: 50 cubits, Height: 30 cubits
Length: 100 cubits, Breadth: 20 cubits, Height: 15 cubits
Length: 500 cubits, Breadth: 100 cubits, Height: 50 cubits
Length: 200 cubits, Breadth: 40 cubits, Height: 25 cubits
questions.correctAnswer: Length: 300 cubits, Breadth: 50 cubits, Height: 30 cubits
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:15 specifies the ark's dimensions as 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high, demonstrating God's precise instructions for Noah's obedience, linking to the building instructions in verses 14 and 16.

questions.question: What features of the ark are described in Genesis 6:16?
options: A window finished above by a cubit, a door in the side, and three stories
A roof made of stone and a single large door
Multiple decks with open sides and no windows
A chimney and a front porch
questions.correctAnswer: A window finished above by a cubit, a door in the side, and three stories
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:16 details that the ark should have a window one cubit high above, a side door, and be built with lower, second, and third stories, emphasizing the careful design for safety and habitability during the flood.

questions.question: How does Genesis 6:13 relate to the condition of the earth described in verses 11 and 12?
options: It declares the end of all flesh because the earth is filled with violence
It promises a new covenant despite the violence
It commands the people to repent to avoid destruction
It describes the earth as peaceful and ready for renewal
questions.correctAnswer: It declares the end of all flesh because the earth is filled with violence
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:13 directly connects to verses 11 and 12 by announcing the impending destruction due to the earth's violence and corruption, confirming God's judgment against all flesh.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:18, who are the individuals God promises to save in the ark?
options: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives
questions.correctAnswer: Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:18 specifies that God will establish a covenant with Noah and save him along with his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives, highlighting the importance of family obedience and trust.

questions.question: What does Genesis 6:19 instruct Noah to do in preparation for the flood?
options: Bring two of every living thing, male and female, into the ark
Build a large city to protect everyone
questions.correctAnswer: Bring two of every living thing, male and female, into the ark
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:19 commands Noah to take pairs of every living creature to preserve life, reinforcing obedience to God’s plan for survival during the coming judgment described in verses 13 and 17.

questions.question: In Genesis 6:20, what kinds of creatures does God specify Noah should bring into the ark?
options: Fowls, cattle, and every creeping thing after their kind
questions.correctAnswer: Fowls, cattle, and every creeping thing after their kind
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:20 details the types of creatures to be saved, including birds (fowls), cattle, and creeping things, each after their kind, showing God's care for all creation.

questions.question: What does Genesis 6:21 say Noah should do concerning food?
options: Gather food to sustain himself and the animals in the ark
Rely on God to provide food during the flood
questions.correctAnswer: Gather food to sustain himself and the animals in the ark
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:21 instructs Noah to collect food for himself and the animals, demonstrating practical preparation and obedience to God's command to ensure survival.

questions.question: How did Noah respond to God's commands according to Genesis 6:22?
options: He did all that God commanded him
He hesitated and doubted God's plan
He built a smaller ark than instructed
questions.correctAnswer: He did all that God commanded him
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:22 confirms Noah's obedience, stating he did everything just as God commanded, highlighting faith and trust in God's word despite the coming flood.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 6:11, the earth was filled with peace and righteousness before God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:11 clearly states the earth was corrupt and filled with violence before God, not peaceful or righteous.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 6:14 teaches us about the importance of obedience and attention to detail in following God's commands.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:14 shows God giving specific instructions about building the ark, illustrating that faithful obedience and careful attention to God's commands are vital, as further evidenced by Noah's compliance in verse 22.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 6.

questions.question: What is the reason God gives for bringing the flood upon the earth?
options: Because the earth was filled with violence
Because the sons of God were righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Because the earth was filled with violence
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:13 states God will destroy all flesh because the earth is filled with violence through them.

questions.question: According to Genesis 6, what material was Noah instructed to use for building the ark?
questions.correctAnswer: Gopher wood
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:14 specifies that Noah was to make the ark of gopher wood.

questions.question: How high above the ark was Noah commanded to make the window?
questions.correctAnswer: One cubit
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:16 says the window shall be finished one cubit above the ark.

questions.question: How many stories was the ark to have according to God's instructions?
questions.correctAnswer: Three stories
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:16 describes the ark as having lower, second, and third stories.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated 'pitch' in Genesis 6:14, used to cover the ark?
options: A type of wood resin used for incense
A form of oil used for anointing
questions.correctAnswer: A waterproof resin or bitumen
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'kopher' translated as 'pitch' in Genesis 6:14 refers to a waterproof resin or bitumen used to seal and waterproof the ark.

questions.question: In Genesis 6:17, what is described as the scope of the flood God will bring?
options: To destroy all flesh with the breath of life from under heaven
Only the wicked men on earth
Only the animals on the earth
Only the earth's plants and vegetation
questions.correctAnswer: To destroy all flesh with the breath of life from under heaven
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:17 says God will bring a flood to destroy all flesh wherein is the breath of life from under heaven.

questions.question: Who does God establish His covenant with in Genesis 6?
questions.correctAnswer: Noah and his family
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:18 states God will establish His covenant with Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons' wives.

questions.question: How many of each kind of living creature was Noah commanded to bring into the ark?
options: Two of every sort, male and female
Seven pairs of clean animals only
questions.correctAnswer: Two of every sort, male and female
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:19 commands Noah to bring two of every living thing, male and female, into the ark.

questions.question: What does Genesis 6:21 instruct Noah to take into the ark besides animals?
options: Food for himself and the animals
questions.correctAnswer: Food for himself and the animals
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:21 tells Noah to gather food that is eaten for himself and the animals.

questions.question: What is the significance of Noah's obedience described in Genesis 6:22?
options: He did all according to God's command
He built the ark with his own plan
questions.correctAnswer: He did all according to God's command
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:22 emphasizes Noah's obedience by stating he did according to all that God commanded him.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the covenant God makes with Noah in Genesis 6:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 9:8-17
questions.explanation: Genesis 9:8-17 records God establishing a covenant with Noah after the flood, echoing the promise in Genesis 6:18.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage refers to the flood in Genesis 6-9 as a type of baptism?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 3:20-21 connects Noah's flood with baptism, showing typology between the flood and salvation through water.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Genesis 6:17-22 regarding the flood narrative?
options: Inclusio framing the judgment and salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the judgment and salvation
questions.explanation: The passage uses inclusio by framing the flood judgment (v.17) and salvation through the ark (v.18-22) to emphasize God's justice and mercy.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 6:20, Noah was to bring seven pairs of every kind of bird into the ark.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:20 states two of every sort of bird, male and female, not seven pairs, were to be brought into the ark.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 6:9 describes Noah as a just man who walked with God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:9 explicitly says Noah was just, perfect in his generations, and walked with God.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Genesis 6:3 reveal about the limitation God places on human lifespan and His interaction with humanity?
options: God limits man's lifespan to 120 years and shows patience by restraining His spirit
God immediately ends human life upon sinning
God grants immortality to the righteous only
God allows humans to live as long as they desire
questions.correctAnswer: God limits man's lifespan to 120 years and shows patience by restraining His spirit
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:3 states that 'My spirit shall not always strive with man' and 'his days shall be an hundred and twenty years,' indicating God limits human lifespan and withholds judgment for a period

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:5, what is the condition of the human heart that leads God to judgment?
options: The imagination of the thoughts of man's heart is only evil continually
Man's heart is full of love and kindness
Man's heart is confused but hopeful
Man's heart is indifferent to sin
questions.correctAnswer: The imagination of the thoughts of man's heart is only evil continually
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:5 highlights that God saw the wickedness and that every imagination of man's heart was continually evil, showing pervasive sinfulness as the cause for judgment

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Genesis 6:6 where God is described as repenting and being grieved?
questions.correctAnswer: God's mercy and relational sorrow
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:6 shows God's relational nature and mercy as He is grieved and repents over creating man, indicating His sorrow over human sin rather than impassibility

questions.question: What theological doctrine is taught in Genesis 6:7 regarding God's actions toward creation?
options: Doctrine of divine judgment through universal destruction
Doctrine of predestination only for the elect
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of divine judgment through universal destruction
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:7 reveals God's decision to destroy man, beast, creeping things, and birds due to wickedness, showing the doctrine of God's righteous judgment upon sin

questions.question: How is Noah described in Genesis 6:9, and what theological significance does this description carry?
options: Noah was just, perfect in his generations, and walked with God, illustrating sanctification and divine favor
Noah was a warrior and conqueror
Noah was a prophet who predicted the flood
Noah was a sinful man who repented late in life
questions.correctAnswer: Noah was just, perfect in his generations, and walked with God, illustrating sanctification and divine favor
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:9 calls Noah just and perfect, walking with God, indicating his righteous character and God's grace amid a corrupt world

questions.question: What does Genesis 6:11 indicate about the state of the earth before the flood, and what implication does this have for biblical theology?
options: The earth was corrupt and filled with violence, highlighting the universal nature of sin
The earth was peaceful and prosperous
The earth was barren and empty
The earth was inhabited only by righteous people
questions.correctAnswer: The earth was corrupt and filled with violence, highlighting the universal nature of sin
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:11 states the earth was corrupt and filled with violence, emphasizing sin's totalizing effect on creation, a key biblical theme

questions.question: According to Genesis 6:14, what specific instructions does God give Noah about the ark, and what does this reveal about divine providence?
options: Make an ark of gopher wood, pitch it inside and out, indicating God's detailed provision for salvation
Build a small boat from reeds for personal escape
Construct a temple as a place of worship
Create a floating island of stones
questions.correctAnswer: Make an ark of gopher wood, pitch it inside and out, indicating God's detailed provision for salvation
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:14 commands Noah to build a specific ark with gopher wood and pitch it, showing God's providential care in delivering Noah and creation

questions.question: What eschatological foreshadowing is found in Genesis 6:17 regarding the flood?
options: A coming judgment that destroys all flesh with life breath, foreshadowing final judgment
A symbolic cleansing of only a city
An eternal curse on the earth
questions.correctAnswer: A coming judgment that destroys all flesh with life breath, foreshadowing final judgment
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:17 speaks of a flood to destroy all flesh with breath of life, typologically pointing to God's ultimate final judgment on sin

questions.question: How does Genesis 6:18 encapsulate the doctrine of covenant in the context of Noah's narrative?
options: God establishes a covenant with Noah and his family as a means of salvation and preservation
God rejects any covenant due to human sinfulness
Noah makes a covenant with animals
The covenant is conditional on human works
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes a covenant with Noah and his family as a means of salvation and preservation
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:18 records God establishing a covenant with Noah and his household, emphasizing divine commitment to salvation amid judgment

questions.question: Considering Genesis 6:19-20, what does the command to bring animals into the ark teach about God's providence and the preservation of creation?
options: God preserves biological kinds through Noah, showing providential care for creation's continuity
God intends to destroy all animals without exception
Animals are irrelevant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves biological kinds through Noah, showing providential care for creation's continuity
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:19-20 commands Noah to bring pairs of animals by kind, demonstrating God's providential preservation of creation's diversity

questions.question: What combined teaching about human sinfulness and divine judgment is conveyed by Genesis 6:5-6 and Genesis 6:12?
options: Human sinfulness is pervasive and corrupts all flesh, which grieves God and leads to judgment
Human sinfulness is minor and ignored by God
Sin has no effect on God's plans
questions.correctAnswer: Human sinfulness is pervasive and corrupts all flesh, which grieves God and leads to judgment
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:5-6 and 6:12 together show that human wickedness corrupted all flesh, causing God's grief and decision to judge, highlighting sin's seriousness

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is gained by synthesizing Genesis 6:8 and Genesis 6:22 about Noah's role in salvation history?
options: Noah's grace before God and obedience exemplify justification and sanctification
Noah was saved by works alone
Noah acted independently of God's will
questions.correctAnswer: Noah's grace before God and obedience exemplify justification and sanctification
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:8 shows Noah found grace, and 6:22 records his obedience, illustrating divine favor and human faithfulness in salvation

questions.question: How does Genesis 6:4 contribute to biblical theology concerning the nature of evil and human history?
options: It mentions giants and mighty men from 'sons of God' and 'daughters of men,' revealing the mixing of divine and human realms and escalating corruption
It denies the existence of evil beings
It speaks only of peaceful coexistence
questions.correctAnswer: It mentions giants and mighty men from 'sons of God' and 'daughters of men,' revealing the mixing of divine and human realms and escalating corruption
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:4 notes giants and men of renown born from divine-human unions, indicating a supernatural dimension to the world's corruption

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Genesis 6:13-17 contradicts modern understanding of animals and flood narratives. What does this passage actually teach about God's judgment and salvation?
options: It teaches God's sovereign judgment via a worldwide flood and provision for survival through the ark, emphasizing divine justice and mercy
It is a myth with no theological meaning
It describes a local flood only
It teaches that animals were not preserved
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches God's sovereign judgment via a worldwide flood and provision for survival through the ark, emphasizing divine justice and mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:13-17 describes God's decision to flood the earth to judge sin and His instructions to Noah to build an ark for preservation, affirming God's righteous and merciful nature

questions.question: What does the combined teaching of Genesis 6:10 and Genesis 6:18 reveal about the continuity of God's covenant promises through human generations?
options: God's covenant includes Noah's sons and their families, highlighting covenantal continuity across generations
God's covenant is limited to Noah alone
God's covenant is conditional on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant includes Noah's sons and their families, highlighting covenantal continuity across generations
questions.explanation: Genesis 6:10 mentions Noah's sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and 6:18 promises covenantal salvation to them and their wives, showing covenantal transmission
